landingSites.name: Apollo 11
landingSites.description: First human lunar landing. Tranquility Base, Neil Armstrong & Buzz Aldrin.

landingSites.name: Apollo 12
landingSites.description: Ocean of Storms, pinpoint landing next to Surveyor 3.

landingSites.name: Apollo 14
landingSites.description: Fra Mauro formation, Alan Shepard & Edgar Mitchell.

landingSites.name: Apollo 15
landingSites.description: Hadley-Apennine region, first Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV).

landingSites.name: Apollo 16
landingSites.description: Descartes Highlands, Cayley formation exploration.

landingSites.name: Apollo 17
landingSites.description: Taurus-Littrow valley, Eugene Cernan & Harrison Schmitt (geologist).

landingSites.name: Luna 2
landingSites.description: First human-made spacecraft to reach the Moon's surface (Mare Imbrium).

landingSites.name: Luna 9
landingSites.description: First survivable soft landing on the Moon (Oceanus Procellarum).

landingSites.name: Luna 16
landingSites.description: First automated robotic sample return from another celestial body (Mare Fecunditatis).

landingSites.name: Luna 17 (Lunokhod 1)
landingSites.description: First successful robotic lunar rover (Mare Imbrium).

landingSites.name: Luna 21 (Lunokhod 2)
landingSites.description: Second robotic Soviet rover (Le Monnier crater).

landingSites.name: Luna 24
landingSites.description: Final Luna mission sample return (Mare Crisium).

landingSites.name: Surveyor 1
landingSites.description: First American soft landing on the Moon (Oceanus Procellarum).

landingSites.name: Surveyor 3
landingSites.description: Visited by Apollo 12 astronauts Pete Conrad and Alan Bean.

landingSites.name: Chang'e 3 (Yutu)
landingSites.description: First Chinese lunar lander & Yutu rover (Mare Imbrium).

landingSites.name: Chang'e 4 (Yutu-2)
landingSites.description: First soft landing on the lunar FAR SIDE (Von Kármán crater, South Pole-Aitken basin).

landingSites.name: Chang'e 5
landingSites.description: Chinese lunar sample return (Mons Rümker, Oceanus Procellarum).

landingSites.name: Chang'e 6
landingSites.description: First ever sample return from the lunar FAR SIDE (Apollo crater basin).

landingSites.name: Chandrayaan-3 (Shiv Shakti)
landingSites.description: First spacecraft to soft-land near the Lunar South Pole region. Vikram lander & Pragyan rover at Shiv Shakti Point.

landingSites.name: SLIM
landingSites.description: Smart Lander for Investigating Moon (Japan), pinpoint landing within 55 meters at Shioli crater.

maria.name: Mare Tranquillitatis
maria.description: Sea of Tranquility. Site of Apollo 11 first moon landing.

maria.name: Mare Serenitatis
maria.description: Sea of Serenity. Prominent circular basin east of Mare Imbrium.

maria.name: Mare Imbrium
maria.description: Sea of Rains. One of the largest impact craters in the Solar System, ringed by mountains.

maria.name: Oceanus Procellarum
maria.description: Ocean of Storms. The largest lunar mare, spanning over 2,500 km across the western near side.

maria.name: Mare Crisium
maria.description: Sea of Crises. Distinct isolated oval basin on the eastern near-side limb.

maria.name: Mare Fecunditatis
maria.description: Sea of Fecundity. Eastern basin containing Messier craters.

maria.name: Mare Nectaris
maria.description: Sea of Nectar. Small circular mare south of Mare Tranquillitatis.

maria.name: Mare Nubium
maria.description: Sea of Clouds. Pre-Imbrian basin southeast of Oceanus Procellarum.

maria.name: Mare Humorum
maria.description: Sea of Moisture. Circular basin bordered by Gassendi crater.

maria.name: Mare Vaporum
maria.description: Sea of Vapors. Located near the center of the lunar disk.

maria.name: Mare Frigoris
maria.description: Sea of Cold. Long arcing band across the far northern near side.

maria.name: Mare Orientale
maria.description: Eastern Sea. Spectacular bullseye multi-ring impact basin on the western limb.

maria.name: Mare Moscoviense
maria.description: Sea of Moscow. Rare dark basaltic mare basin on the lunar far side.

maria.name: Mare Ingenii
maria.description: Sea of Cleverness. Located in the southern far-side hemisphere.

craters.name: Tycho
craters.description: Prominent young impact crater with ray system extending over 1,500 km across the near side.

craters.name: Copernicus
craters.description: Archetypal impact crater with terraced walls, multiple central peaks, and extensive bright rays.

craters.name: Kepler
craters.description: Bright rayed crater in Oceanus Procellarum named after Johannes Kepler.

craters.name: Aristarchus
craters.description: Brightest major geological formation on the Moon, with an albedo nearly double the average.

craters.name: Plato
craters.description: Dark lava-flooded crater on the northern border of Mare Imbrium.

craters.name: Archimedes
craters.description: Large flat-floored crater in eastern Mare Imbrium.

craters.name: Clavius
craters.description: One of the largest craters on the Moon, featuring a curved chain of diminishing sub-craters.

craters.name: Eratosthenes
craters.description: Well-defined crater marking the western terminus of the Montes Apenninus.

craters.name: Ptolemaeus
craters.description: Ancient pre-Imbrian walled plain near the central meridian.

craters.name: Alphonsus
craters.description: Famous crater with central peak and dark mantle pyroclastic deposits (possible lunar volcanism).

craters.name: Theophilus
craters.description: Prominent crater with high triple central peaks on the northwest edge of Mare Nectaris.

craters.name: Langrenus
craters.description: Prominent impact crater near the eastern limb with complex terraced walls.

craters.name: Grimaldi
craters.description: Near the western limb, notable for having one of the darkest basaltic floors on the Moon.

craters.name: Gassendi
craters.description: Large floor-fractured crater on the northern edge of Mare Humorum with complex rilles.

craters.name: Tsiolkovskiy
craters.description: Spectacular far-side crater with intensely dark mare floor and brilliant white central peak.

craters.name: Jackson
craters.description: Far-side rayed crater with asymmetric ray system visible from lunar orbit.

craters.name: Shackleton
craters.description: Lunar South Pole crater whose permanently shadowed interior contains water ice deposits.

mountains.name: Montes Apenninus
mountains.description: Spectacular rugged mountain range rising up to 5,000 m above Mare Imbrium.

mountains.name: Montes Caucasus
mountains.description: Rugged range separating Mare Imbrium from Mare Serenitatis.

mountains.name: Montes Alpes
mountains.description: Northern mountain range bisected by the dramatic Vallis Alpes (Alpine Valley).

mountains.name: Mons Huygens
mountains.description: Highest mountain peak on the Moon, located in Montes Apenninus.

mountains.name: Mons Hadley
mountains.description: Towering peak in Montes Apenninus bordering Rima Hadley and the Apollo 15 landing site.

mountains.name: Mons Rümker
mountains.description: Volcanic complex in Oceanus Procellarum, site of the Chang'e 5 landing.
